sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change Request Number 2015-011: retire [xip] Xipináwa (non-existent), adopted 2016-01-15. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 2: 'The Ethnologue has no information on Xipináwa [xip], except for a referenct to "SIL 1976." Loukotka (1968:172) indicates that this language is unattested. Citing this same source, Hammarstrom (2015) states that Xipináwa cannot be asserted to have been a separate language. Fleck (2013) does not list it in his complete list of living and extinct Panoan languages.'

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH. pp. 14, 89, 109.

sources.note: Nothing. 'Shipinawa' appears only in Table 2 'Tentative Classification of Possibly Panoan Languages/Dialects Lacking Linguistic Data' (p. 14, II.C.vii.a Chama subgroup: 'Shipinawa – Shipibo dialect (Velasco, 1988 [1788–1789]: 546)'), in the name index (p. 89: variants Chepenagua, Chipinawa, Sipinawa, Šipinawa) and in the location list (p. 109: upper Liberdade and Valparaiso Rs, right-bank affluents of the Juruá, Brazil, after Linhares 1913 apud Rivet & Tastevin 1921: 472; Tastevin 1919: 146). No wordlist, no phonology.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages (Reference Series 7). Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 172 (Pano stock, Tropical Forest group).
